text:
jordan_acme: Hey team — our nightly migration started at ~02:00 UTC and after about 10k requests we began getting 429s. We just switched from free -> paid but the upgrade is blocked by a billing hold. Can we get a temporary burst or guidance?

alex_support: Sorry about that, Jordan. Can you paste one of the failing request IDs and the response headers (x-rate-limit-*, x-request-id) if you have them? Also what concurrency are you running?

jordan_acme: Concurrency is 12 workers hitting /v1/completions. Sample response body and headers:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: rQn3k-9h4
x-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1680003600
{
  "error": {"message": "Rate limit exceeded"}
}
```
Repro steps: 1) start 12 parallel processes hitting batch of 50 prompts each; 2) keep token length ~300; 3) runs for ~15m then 429s.

alex_support: Thanks — those headers show you hit your per-minute window. Two immediate options: reduce concurrency to ~4-6 and add exponential backoff (start 500ms) or we can open a temporary burst. I can request a 24-hour burst while billing is sorted.

deploy-bot: Automated note: customer rQn3k-9h4 triggered quota guardrail. Current plan: Free -> Pending paid. Burst requests require billing clearance or manual ops override.

maria_billing: Jordan — I see an unpaid invoice (INV-2024-117) blocking account state changes. Until that settles our automated flow won't accept the plan change. Link to pay: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/INV-2024-117. If you can share the payment confirmation or PO, we can clear the hold faster.

jordan_acme: We're working on the PO but can you do a short burst in the meantime? Migration must finish tonight.

sam_sales: @maria_billing I can route a priority review if Jordan shares the PO or a payment screenshot. Jordan — I can also temporarily authorize an ops escalation to unblock for up to 24h if you confirm the migration ETA and expected token throughput. How long to finish at reduced concurrency (~6)?

jordan_acme: At concurrency 6 it'll take ~9 hours. With allowed burst we can finish in ~3 hours. ETA now ~03:30 UTC if we get it.

alex_support: Okay — documenting request: temporary burst for account acme-inc, reason: production data migration, requested window: 3 hours. I'll ask ops to apply manual override. Please switch to concurrency 6 and enable 1s jittered backoff as a precaution. Example backoff snippet:```js
async function sendWithBackoff(req) {
  for (let i=0;i<5;i++) {
    try { return await client.create(req) }
    catch (e) { await sleep(Math.pow(2,i)*500 + Math.random()*200) }
  }
  throw new Error('rate-limited');
}
```

maria_billing: Confirmed: once we receive a PO or payment screenshot we'll clear the billing hold. I queued the invoice for expedited processing.

sam_sales: I have notified the sales manager and will join the ops call. @alex_support can you file the ops override ticket (OPS-8942) and request a 12k token/minute burst for 3 hours?

alex_support: Filed OPS-8942 and requested manual override. Ops approved a temporary 3-hour burst window (start now). Please confirm when you resume and paste any new 429 headers if they reappear.

jordan_acme: Resuming now at concurrency 6. Will post if anything else pops. Really appreciate the quick help. :pray:

alex_support: Great — monitoring. If you still see 429s, paste the x-request-id. Also consider increasing client-side caching of repeated prompts to reduce token load.

jordan_acme: All green so far, migration cutover completed at 03:14 UTC. No more 429s after the override. Will clear invoice today. Thanks everyone! :tada:

maria_billing: Thanks Jordan — let us know when payment/PO is uploaded and I'll confirm the account state update.

sam_sales: Follow-up: I'll reach out to Jordan for a quick post-mortem and discuss a Dedicated plan to avoid future migration pain.

alex_support: Closing thread on our side but OPS ticket will remain in case of follow-up. Keep us posted.
